checklist.item: Secrets and server texts (tokens, header values, SMTP or upstream replies, file contents) in errors, logs and responses.
checklist.evidence: Settings errors with a marker in 25 hostile values (PULSE_API_URL with user info, query, other scheme or junk; PULSE_PROBE_TOKEN with control or non-ASCII characters; both token settings at once; token file missing, a directory, empty, two lines, control characters, a symlink to /proc/self/environ; PULSE_LOCATION, PULSE_CHECKS_RELOAD_MS, buffer settings, PULSE_LOG_LEVEL, PULSE_HEALTH_PORT, PULSE_PROBE_BLOCK_PRIVATE_RANGES, five malformed PULSE_PROBE_HEADER_HOSTS): every one a StartupError, marker=false in 25 of 25. Invalid api checks with a marker in a header value, in URL user info and in a body: skip lines name the field only ('checks[2].headers.x-k: must be at most 4096 visible ASCII/obs-text characters or spaces', 'checks[4].url: must not contain a username or password'), markerInLog false. Running service, 60 s at PULSE_LOG_LEVEL=debug: grep -c <token> over the log = 0. Result reasons for hostile targets: 'ERR_SSL_WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER' (TLS check vs text server), 'Malformed_HTTP_Response' (garbage status line with a marker), 'DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT', 'json: invalid body'; no marker in any reason. /metrics holds check ids only; hostile ids are escaped (0 injected lines). Findings: security-probe-2026-11-04-3, -4.

checklist.item: Authentication before any other check; status codes and their order on admin routes.
checklist.evidence: probe has no admin or authenticated routes; its only listener is the pulse-kit ops listener, unauthenticated by design. Observed with curl -X <method> on the running service: GET /healthz, /readyz, /metrics -> 200; HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE, PATCH on these paths and every method on / and /admin -> 404 (methodNotAllowed '404', src/main.ts:99). Absolute-form request target -> 404; /metrics/../healthz with --path-as-is -> 404; /metrics?x=1 -> 200.

checklist.item: Body and size limits on every method, also before any write.
checklist.evidence: Ops listener (bun pid RSS): POST /healthz with 100 MB -> 404 at once, 0 bytes uploaded; 3x GET /metrics with a 500 MB body -> 200, drained not buffered (RSS 66104 kB before, 66280 kB after); GET /healthz with a 500 MB chunked body -> 200; 64 KB header -> 431; 4 KB path -> 404; /healthz still 200. No request makes the service write. Api: endless body on GET /probe/checks -> 'response is larger than 5242880 bytes' after 9 ms, RSS +15 MB. Check targets: endless body without keyword -> up in 2 ms, RSS +4 MB; keyword never present -> 'keyword "never-there" not found' after 5 ms, RSS +9 MB (1 MiB cap, src/check.ts:27); jsonAssert -> 'json: invalid body' after 3 ms; body trickled 1 byte per 200 ms with timeoutMs 1000 -> 'timeout after 1000ms' after 1001 ms. RDAP caps 1 MiB and 2 MiB (src/check-domain.ts:59, :60). POST /results answer body cancelled (src/client.ts:396). The token file is read whole without a cap (operator file).

checklist.item: Input validation at every trust boundary; validators never throw on any input type.
checklist.evidence: Contract validateCheck with undefined, null, BigInt, Symbol, function, a getter object, a Proxy whose traps all throw, a 100,000-deep array, an own __proto__ key and an id object with toString: none throws; all invalid except the __proto__ cases (accepted, see security-probe-2026-11-04-5). parseHeaderHosts with 10 texts (unset, empty, {}, [], null, 1, a string, wrong value types, duplicate keys) and, through loadSettings, a 30,000-deep array and an __proto__ key: StartupError or an empty or valid map, never another throw. Env settings validated at startup (row 1). Check URLs must be http(s) without user info (contract src/schema.ts:35); the probe re-checks the scheme per hop (src/check.ts:427); env header values pass headerValueSchema (src/client.ts:168). Finding: missing startup validation before using the location in an outbound header (security-probe-2026-11-04-1); private reproduction details withheld.

checklist.item: No accessor or getter of untrusted input runs.
checklist.evidence: All untrusted data enters as text through JSON.parse: the api check list (contract fetchJson), jsonAssert and RDAP bodies (src/check.ts:344, src/check-domain.ts:122) and PULSE_PROBE_HEADER_HOSTS (src/header-hosts.ts:192). JSON.parse creates data properties only. The contract validator gave 'c.url: is required' for an object whose url is a getter, with 0 getter runs. probe reads raw.id (src/client.ts:235) and walks JSON pointers with Object.hasOwn (src/check.ts:313), both on JSON.parse values only.

checklist.item: SSRF: allowed targets, environment lookups, redirects (cross-origin, https to http), forwarded headers.
checklist.evidence: With PULSE_PROBE_BLOCK_PRIVATE_RANGES and the real guard (real fetch, lookupAll, TCP, TLS, DNS): 13 loopback and unspecified spellings in HTTP URLs (decimal, hex, octal, short, IPv4-mapped, trailing dot, localhost, 0, [::]) all blocked, 0 requests at the local server; TCP and TLS hosts in 11 spellings (brackets, %zone, leading space, 127.1, 0x7f000001) all blocked; DNS resolvers 127.0.0.53, ::1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 10.0.0.1 all blocked; redirect hops from an allowed host to loopback, localhost, octal, IPv4-mapped and metadata addresses all 'redirect blocked', 1 request (first hop only). ::ffff:0:7f00:1 and 64:ff9b::7f00:1 not blocked (note N8). Checks with an env header, a literal authorization header or a POST body, redirected with 301/302/303/307/308 to another port or host name: 30 of 30 down 'not followed', 0 requests and 0 leaks at the other origin. Api calls: Bun drops Authorization on every cross-origin hop (authHasToken false in all cases), but the client follows redirects to another origin and from https to http, and 307/308 re-post the result there (security-probe-2026-11-04-2). Environment lookups: env header values are read only for PULSE_HEADER_* names bound to the check host (src/client.ts:148, :156); Bun fetch uses HTTP_PROXY for api calls too (note N1). Forwarded headers: not applicable; probe sends none, and the ops listener reads only the method and path (kit src/ops-server.ts:57).

probe writes no files: grep -nE 'writeFile|appendFile|openSync|createWriteStream|mkdir|rename|Bun\.write|unlink|node:fs' src/*.ts (tests excluded) finds only src/main.ts:1 (readFileSync for the token file). Results are buffered in memory only.

checklist.item: Dependencies, Docker base images and CI actions pinned and approved (docs/approved-packages.md).
checklist.evidence: package.json: contract and kit by full SHA; dev @biomejs/biome 2.6.3, lefthook 2.2.2, @types/node 26.6.6, @types/bun 1.4.0, typescript7 npm:typescript@7.0.2, pulse-config by full SHA. Runtime dependencies and listed dev versions match the approved list; shared pulse-config tooling has no standalone package row (note N4). bun.lock has an integrity hash per git dependency. Image node_modules: @lorenzh/pulse-contract, @lorenzh/pulse-kit, zod only. bun audit: exit 1, 1 moderate advisory in a dev-only package (note N2). Docker: both stages oven/bun:1.4.0-alpine@sha256:07235578...437eb (approved); docker buildx imagetools inspect shows the tag at the same digest; image runs as uid=1000(bun), holds src, package.json, node_modules, 0 test files, no git, Cmd bun --no-env-file src/main.ts. Build: bun install --frozen-lockfile --production --ignore-scripts; apk add git unpinned (note N3). CI: ci.yml permissions contents: read; docker job actions/checkout@3d3c42e... (v7.0.1, approved target pin) with persist-credentials: false; check and release call pulse-config 04108fa..., whose check.yml and release.yml use checkout 3d3c42e... with persist-credentials: false, setup-bun 0c5077e..., attest 1e69f48..., buildkit v0.34.1@sha256:99368f3e..., all approved.

findings.title: An accepted location setting makes every HTTP check report down
findings.class: Missing startup validation before using an environment setting in an outbound HTTP header
findings.command: Withheld under the public security disclosure rule; SEC-1 was independently rebuilt and reproduced outside the repository by audit-review.
findings.excerpt: SEC-1 expectation exit 1: settings accepted; HTTP down 3/3, TCP up 3/3; control HTTP up; graceful service shutdown exit 0. Input and reproduction procedure withheld.
findings.impact: Some documented location names accepted at startup make every HTTP check report down with only 'request error'. This creates false incidents with one location and false down votes that can affect quorum with several. Also src/location.ts:14 and src/check.ts:502. The review independently confirmed the failure against local peers.
findings.fixDirection: Validate PULSE_LOCATION against its downstream header encoding at startup, with exit 2 and a message naming the setting, or safely encode the location before forming the user-agent header. Document the accepted values.

findings.title: The api client follows redirects to another origin and from https to http
findings.class: SSRF and downgrade via redirect on the api connection
findings.command: timeout 30 bun --no-env-file /tmp/probe-audit-review.XEh6U8/review.ts sec2 (temporary harness; deleted after review)
findings.excerpt: Reviewer: redirects 307 and 308 each give outcome=accepted, postsAtOtherOrigin=1, authorization=null, resultBodyPreserved=true; cross-origin checks GET followed=true; HTTPS to HTTP checks redirect followed=true, authorization=null. Audit service run: 6 redirected posts counted as ok.
findings.impact: Whoever can make the api origin or a proxy in front of it answer with a redirect makes the probe deliver results elsewhere while counting them delivered, and read its check list from another host or over plain http, where a network attacker can choose the probe's targets. Env header secrets stay bound to their hosts. Also src/client.ts:281 and contract src/client.ts:130 (no redirect option).
findings.fixDirection: Use redirect 'error' (or 'manual' and treat 3xx as a failure) on POST /results, and give fetchJson a fetch that does the same (or add the option to the contract client).

findings.title: Text of an api response body reaches the log
findings.command: timeout 30 bun --no-env-file /tmp/probe-audit-review.XEh6U8/review.ts sec3 (temporary harness; deleted after review)
findings.excerpt: loadChecks: invalid JSON: JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "review_upstream_marker_699"; markerInLog=true; startup retry log contains upstream response text
findings.impact: A token from the api or a proxy reply can land in the probe log when the body has a bare word at the first invalid position. Logged by src/client.ts:372 at startup and src/reloader.ts:50 on reload. HTTP checks avoid this on purpose (src/check.ts:346).
findings.fixDirection: Map invalid-json to a fixed text such as 'invalid JSON', like the http and too-large cases.

findings.title: The id of an invalid check is logged without a length cap
findings.command: timeout 30 bun --no-env-file /tmp/probe-audit-review.XEh6U8/review.ts sec4 (temporary harness; deleted after review)
findings.excerpt: Reviewer: bodyBytes=1300041; skipLogLines=4; lineLengths=1000052,100052,100052,100052; longestLogLine=1000052. Audit fixture: 1000051,100051,100051,100051 for 1300157 bytes. The review uses a smaller invalid-record fixture; both results show the full id is logged.
findings.impact: A hostile or broken api can write up to the 5 MiB body cap into the log per load; the logged-id memory resets after 10,000 ids, so many distinct ids can repeat on reloads. The comment at src/client.ts:179 treats such an api as hostile for the dedupe keys only.
findings.fixDirection: Cut the id in the log line (for example with quote from src/reason.ts), or log its hash or position.

findings.title: A header named __proto__ is dropped without a log line
findings.class: Plain object used as a header map
findings.command: timeout 30 bun --no-env-file /tmp/probe-audit-review.XEh6U8/review.ts sec5 (temporary harness; deleted after review)
findings.impact: The configured header is missing from every request; no prototype changes. Also src/check.ts:556.
findings.fixDirection: Build the header map with Object.create(null) or a Map, or reject the name in the contract.

review.scope: Probe clone HEAD matches the audited commit. The audit's meta commit is the parent of the report commit, with no change to docs/approved-packages.md. Dependency clone HEADs are newer; temporary copies were fetched and checked out at the reported contract, kit and config pins. Installed contract and kit src trees match those pinned copies (diff -qr exit 0). All attacks used local peers.
review.result: All five findings reproduced; none removed or regraded. One P2, four P3, four candidates. SEC-1 remains P2 because accepted documented settings can break all HTTP checks; SEC-2 through SEC-4 require a hostile or broken API response, and SEC-5 requires an unusual header name. P2 trigger, payload and procedure removed from both public files, including the checklist. No audit gate remains.

checks.excerpt: JSON/Markdown: 5 identical findings, ids, titles and severities; 8 matching checklist items/statuses; required fields present; 4 candidates; commit SHAs match

checks.command: timeout 300 bun run check (unchanged temporary probe copy)
checks.excerpt: pulse-workflows: ok (1 files, 3 uses); typecheck passed; 419 pass, 0 fail; 99.46% line coverage. Existing lint warnings and infos only. Includes secret redaction, API size/time bounds, private-range guards, environment host bindings, redirects and RDAP behavior.

checks.command: SEC-1 private expectation test; command withheld under the public security disclosure rule
checks.excerpt: Settings accepted; direct HTTP down; service HTTP down 3/3 and TCP up 3/3; control HTTP up; graceful shutdown exit 0; token in logs=false. Input and procedure withheld.

validateCheck hostile types=11; throws=0; getterCalls=0; parseHeaderHosts texts=10; StartupError=7; unexpectedThrows=0; ops method/path matrix=40; expectedStatusCodes=40; ops methods with 16 MiB bodies=8; GET 200, other methods 404; health after requests=200

Only token-file reads and their injected reader appear in settings.ts, token.ts and main.ts; no filesystem writes. The no-admin-routes exclusion also holds after inspecting main.ts and the pinned kit ops handler.
minimatch@10.2.6: 1 moderate advisory, GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, in the development toolchain; confirms N2. Package and workflow pins were also compared with docs/approved-packages.md.

review.limitations: The reviewer did not rebuild Docker or repeat every audit input matrix; Docker conclusions retain the audit's recorded build evidence and were checked against the pinned source. Private expectation harnesses are temporary and deleted after review; they are not committed. API HTTPS downgrade was tested only against a local self-signed server with certificate verification disabled in that test client. No production endpoints were contacted.

notes: N1: Bun's fetch uses HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY for the api calls too; a local proxy listener saw 'GET http://192.0.2.10:8080/probe/checks HTTP/1.1 | Authorization: Bearer <token>'. The docs mention the proxy only for checks (docs/configuration.md:290).
N2: bun audit (exit 1): minimatch@10.2.6, moderate, GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, dev-only through the pulse-config ESLint toolchain; not in the image.
N3: Dockerfile:2 runs apk add --no-cache git without a version pin in the build stage only; the final image has no git.
N4: pulse-config is a dev dependency by git SHA but is not listed as an internal package in docs/approved-packages.md.
N5: contract, kit and config pins are 9, 7 and 2 commits behind main; the newer contract validator change does not affect probe, which passes only JSON.parse output.
N6: the ops listener has no authentication; the image binds it to 0.0.0.0:9100 (Dockerfile:10); it shows check ids, counters and the readiness reason only.
N7: a jsonAssert reason quotes the found body value, cut to 80 characters, by design (docs/configuration.md:114).
N8: ::ffff:0:0/96 (IPv4-translated) is not blocked and not named in the docs; a connect to ::ffff:0:7f00:1 here gave ECONNREFUSED and did not reach a 127.0.0.1 listener.
N9: an api 301/302/303 to another origin on POST /results makes fetch send GET /results there; the result is dropped as rejected. The fix for security-probe-2026-11-04-2 also covers this case.
